transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2025-09-25 14:00 PDT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Recording ID: ff-20250925-7f3b
Attendees: Grace (Redwood AE), Marco (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood CSM), Oliver (Sentinel VP Eng), Maya (Sentinel SRE), Liam (Sentinel Legal), Zara (Sentinel PM)

Summary: quick closure/triage after last week's production incident where requests to the inference pool hit transient KV cache exhaustion causing elevated tail latency and two brief 503 windows. Today we walk the RCA, agree mitigations, owners, and post-incident actions incl SLA credits and verification plan.

Topics: RCA highlights, mitigation patches, rollout & rollback playbook, bench/validation plan, legal/SLA follow-up, next steps

[00:00] Grace: alright folks, um thanks for joining on short notice, I know this is a lot, we'll try and keep to 45, 50 minutes, go through the RCA and then assign owners.
[00:18] Oliver: thanks, appreciate it. Maya and I joined so we can validate the mitigations, and Liam is on for the SLA/legal bits.
[00:26] Maya: and hi, quick note, we did one replay in staging last night where we simulated the high prefix-sharing workload, saw the cache fill pattern similar to prod.
[00:40] Marco: cool, I'll jump in on the repro we built, but first the short RCA synopsis: on 2025-09-18 at ~10:12 UTC the inference runtime started dropping requests as the KV-edge cache hit cache-eviction storms when multiple multitenant prefix sequences converged, this increased memory pressure and triggered the eviction-led thrash, uh leading to GPU worker restarts and a small window of degraded responses.
[01:05] Maya: quick clarification - when you say "KV-edge" you mean the prefix KV store in the serving runtime, right?
[01:12] Marco: yeah, sorry, luv-- it's the per-worker prefix kv cache; sometimes the export transcribes as K V cache. the core issue was an under-sized shard config combined with a new batcher change that increased active sequence count.
[01:28] Oliver: timeline question — how long was the elevated tail latency? customers saw errors for around what, 7 minutes?
[01:34] Priya: our tracking shows two windows, first at 10:12–10:18 and a second blip at ~10:21 for about 2 minutes. overall impact for most tenants was ~9 minutes but big customers saw more replays.
[01:52] Liam: from a legal/SLA perspective, we need the precise minute-level timeline and a statement of what mitigations were performed during the incident.
[02:03] Grace: sure, we'll include that in the RCA doc — Marco already has the artifact, link shared in chat: https://redwood.internal/docs/sentinel-rca-v1 (note: internal link).
[02:18] Marco: jumping into the technical repro: we created a workload generator that replays prefix-heavy sessions with variable sequence lengths; when run at 70–80% of expected concurrency it triggers the same eviction pattern. reproducer is in the shared folder: /bench/sentinel/repro-2025-09-24.sh
[02:40] Maya: hm, I remember last time there was talk about batcher changes, which PR changed the batching window?
[02:48] Marco: PR #3489 adjusted the batch assembly heuristics to greedily pack shorter contexts, that pushed up the active token window slightly; in normal ops it's fine, but with the shard config we had (shard size=256MB) it lowered the eviction threshold.
[03:10] Oliver: does the runtime have an auto-throttle when eviction rate climbs?
[03:14] Marco: not exactly auto-throttle, we have an eviction backoff but it was tuned for different memory patterns; it didn't catch this cross-tenant prefix storm pattern.
[03:30] Grace: ok so root causes as we see them: 1) shard config too small for mixed long-short sequence workloads, 2) batching heuristic change increased active sequence concurrency, 3) monitoring alert thresholds didn't surface the early eviction trend.
[03:50] Maya: agree with that triage. one more operational note: our readiness probe didn't fail-fast for worker-level memory pressure so restart timings were slower — we saw ~18s before the worker restarted.
[04:06] Marco: yes, also we had a related configuration drift: the production pool had an old kernel profile that doesn't include the new eviction metrics; that made the dashboards misleading.
[04:20] Liam: legally, we'll need a clear statement of what was done to prevent recurrence and what customer-facing remediation (SLA credit) will look like.
[04:30] Grace: understood, we'll draft a customer summary.
[04:35] Marco: proposed mitigations — short term: increase shard size for affected pool from 256MB to 1GB, revert the aggressive batcher heuristic to prior behavior or toggle a canary flag, and add a guardrail that rejects/queues requests when eviction rate exceeds threshold. medium term: add sequence-aware batching and a more conservative eviction-policy, and long term: adaptive shard sizing per-tenant.
[04:58] Oliver: can we do increase shard size immediately? what's the risk?
[05:04] Marco: low risk, but it requires a rolling restart of worker pods to pick up the new config; with our current rollout time it's about 10 minutes of progressive restarts, we can do it during low traffic windows, less than a 1% tilt in latency for a minute.
[05:20] Maya: we tried a canary in staging last night and saw the eviction curve flatten within 3 minutes.
[05:28] Grace: good. Liam, any concerns about the rolling restart from legal or compliance?
[05:33] Liam: from legal perspective it's operational, no issue as long as there's a communicated maintenance window; also confirm data retention is not affected.
[05:42] Marco: no data retention changes.
[05:45] [06:00] (crosstalk) 
[06:18] Marco: next, monitoring: we will add an early-warning metric for eviction-rate-per-shard and a derived alert that fires before the eviction threshold hits critical. also will add a runbook 'eviction-thrash-playbook' to the SRE wiki.
[06:40] Maya: please include steps for quick capacity increase and for triggering model fallbacks to smaller-quantized model variant if eviction persists.
[06:52] Marco: yep, fallback flow: when eviction rate > X for Y seconds, use model-variant: quantized-lite with lower KV footprint and route new sessions to it; we'll add telemetry for successful fallbacks.
[07:12] Grace: customer comms — Priya, what's the plan to notify customers?
[07:18] Priya: we'll send an executive summary with the timeline and immediate mitigations (shard increase + batcher toggle), then follow with the full RCA and remediation plan. also include the proposed SLA credit and contact for questions.
[07:34] Liam: for SLA credit, we need the exact impacted tenants list and minute-level graphs; can Redwood provide per-tenant token counts and error windows?
[07:44] Marco: yes, we can pull per-tenant logs and token metrics, though some naming was obfuscated in the logs; we can map tenant IDs to customer IDs and provide graphs.
[07:58] Oliver: one ask from our infra team — can you provide the precise config diff you plan to roll (shard size, kernel profile id, batcher flag) so we can run a pre-approval?
[08:10] Marco: will do, I'll attach the diff and the staging test output.
[08:18] Grace: ok let's talk schedule — short-term mitigation (shard bump + batcher flag revert) we can do in a controlled rollout tomorrow 2025-09-26 in a low-traffic window, Marco to own. medium-term infra changes (monitoring, runbook) target two weeks.
[08:34] Maya: staging validation steps: run the repro at 80% concurrency, run blue-green with canary 10% traffic, validate eviction metric stability for 30 minutes.
[08:46] Marco: noted. I'll create a detailed bench plan and scripts in the shared folder.
[08:52] [09:00] (slight pause)
[09:12] Priya: wanted to call out customer impact scoring; we propose to use our incident severity matrix and then calculate SLA credit per the contract. we'll include a line item for possible credits in the summary.
[09:28] Liam: please also include a statement on whether logs retained any PII or sensitive health data during the incident; that affects notification templates.
[09:38] Marco: confirmed logs did not capture full user prompt payloads due to redaction layer, we only have token counts and metadata.
[09:48] Grace: great. now open questions — prioritized: 1) who runs the staggered rollout tomorrow? 2) what's our verification gate? 3) legal signoff for credit wording.
[10:06] Oliver: we want an on-call window during rollout in case we need immediate rollback.
[10:11] Marco: agreed, I'll be on-call and will stream logs to the shared channel. rollback is a single flag flip plus restart which is about 6 minutes to revert.
[10:24] Grace: okay let's capture owners in the action items.
[10:30] Marco: small detail — the repro indicates a secondary failure path when multiple model-variants are requested in quick succession; we should add a guard that prevents cross-variant warmups causing extra memory allocations.
[10:46] Maya: add that to medium-term improvements.
[10:50] Grace: any further legal concerns Liam?
[10:54] Liam: none at the moment, just want the final draft before we send to customers.
[11:00] Zara: quick product note — customers also asked for a per-tenant health API so they can detect degraded states, is that on roadmap?
[11:10] Grace: we can scope it as an enhancement, probably medium priority; Marco will sketch an API contract and sample responses.
[11:20] Marco: yep, will add apidoc to the follow-up.
[11:26] (silence)
[11:40] Grace: OK let's recap — recap: immediate: shard size bump + batcher flag revert (Marco), staging verification (Maya/Marco), share RCA and customer summary (Grace), SLA credit process (Priya/Liam), bench plan and repro (Marco). medium: monitoring/alerts and runbook (Marco), fallback model flows (Marco), per-tenant health API spec (Marco).
[12:05] Grace: we'll target the follow-up check-in for week of Oct 6 to validate mitigation. I'll send calendar invite.
[12:14] Oliver: thanks everyone.
[12:18] Priya: thanks, we'll keep you posted.
[12:22] End of recording.

Artifacts referenced: https://redwood.internal/docs/sentinel-rca-v1, /bench/sentinel/repro-2025-09-24.sh, PR#3489, eviction-thrash-playbook (SRE wiki)

Customer-facing summary (to be drafted): 1) timeline and impact, 2) immediate mitigations performed, 3) verification steps, 4) next steps and SLA credit proposal.

Notes about transcript quality: several technical terms mangled by auto-transcription ("K V cache" for KV cache, "batcher" sometimes captured as "bacher"), speaker overlaps at 09:00–09:10.
